```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(gridExtra)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(plotly)
library(scales)
library(viridis)
```

Desarrollar como en la demás distribuciones, incluyendo la función de probabilidad y la función de distribución, gráficas considerando el cambio en los parámetros de la distribución. Características de la distribución (media, varianza, moda, cv). Un ejemplo con valores simulados y la verificación del teorema central del límite. Tomar como referencia principal el libro Introducción a la Probabilidad de Luis Rincón, páginas 278-281.

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Funciones con la parametrización del libro: Weibull(alpha, lambda)
# R usa shape = alpha, scale = 1/lambda
# ---------------------------------------------------------
dweib <- function(x, alpha, lambda) dweibull(x, shape = alpha, scale = 1 / lambda)
pweib <- function(q, alpha, lambda) pweibull(q, shape = alpha, scale = 1 / lambda)
qweib <- function(p, alpha, lambda) qweibull(p, shape = alpha, scale = 1 / lambda)
rweib <- function(n, alpha, lambda) rweibull(n, shape = alpha, scale = 1 / lambda)

# Verificación con el ejemplo del libro (R: shape = 8, scale = 2  <=>  alpha = 8, lambda = 0.5)
dweibull(2, 8, 2)     # 1.471518
pweibull(2, 8, 2)     # 0.6321206
pweib(2, 8, 0.5)      # 0.6321206 (misma probabilidad, notación del libro)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Función de densidad: f(x) = alpha * lambda^alpha * x^(alpha-1) * exp(-(lambda*x)^alpha)
#    Cambio en los parámetros (como en la Figura 3.18 del libro)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
cols <- c("black", "red", "blue", "darkgreen", "orange")

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

# (a) lambda = 1 fijo, alpha variable
alphas <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5)
curve(dweib(x, alphas[1], 1), from = 0.01, to = 3, ylim = c(0, 2),
      col = cols[1], lwd = 2, xlab = "x", ylab = "f(x)",
      main = "Densidad Weibull, lambda = 1")
for (i in 2:length(alphas)) curve(dweib(x, alphas[i], 1), add = TRUE, col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = paste("alpha =", alphas), col = cols, lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)

# (b) alpha = 2 fijo, lambda variable
lambdas <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3)
curve(dweib(x, 2, lambdas[1]), from = 0, to = 4, ylim = c(0, 2.2),
      col = cols[1], lwd = 2, xlab = "x", ylab = "f(x)",
      main = "Densidad Weibull, alpha = 2")
for (i in 2:length(lambdas)) curve(dweib(x, 2, lambdas[i]), add = TRUE, col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = paste("lambda =", lambdas), col = cols, lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Función de distribución: F(x) = 1 - exp(-(lambda*x)^alpha), x > 0
# ---------------------------------------------------------
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

curve(pweib(x, alphas[1], 1), from = 0, to = 3, ylim = c(0, 1),
      col = cols[1], lwd = 2, xlab = "x", ylab = "F(x)",
      main = "Distribución Weibull, lambda = 1")
for (i in 2:length(alphas)) curve(pweib(x, alphas[i], 1), add = TRUE, col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
legend("bottomright", legend = paste("alpha =", alphas), col = cols, lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)

curve(pweib(x, 2, lambdas[1]), from = 0, to = 4, ylim = c(0, 1),
      col = cols[1], lwd = 2, xlab = "x", ylab = "F(x)",
      main = "Distribución Weibull, alpha = 2")
for (i in 2:length(lambdas)) curve(pweib(x, 2, lambdas[i]), add = TRUE, col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
legend("bottomright", legend = paste("lambda =", lambdas), col = cols, lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Características de la distribución
#    Media    = Gamma(1 + 1/alpha) / lambda
#    Varianza = [Gamma(1 + 2/alpha) - Gamma(1 + 1/alpha)^2] / lambda^2
#    Moda     = (1/lambda) * ((alpha - 1)/alpha)^(1/alpha)  si alpha > 1; 0 si alpha <= 1
#    CV       = sd / media = sqrt(Gamma(1+2/alpha) - Gamma(1+1/alpha)^2) / Gamma(1+1/alpha)
#               (no depende de lambda)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
carac_weibull <- function(alpha, lambda) {
  g1 <- gamma(1 + 1 / alpha)
  g2 <- gamma(1 + 2 / alpha)
  g3 <- gamma(1 + 3 / alpha)
  media <- g1 / lambda
  varia <- (g2 - g1^2) / lambda^2
  moda  <- if (alpha > 1) (1 / lambda) * ((alpha - 1) / alpha)^(1 / alpha) else 0
  data.frame(alpha = alpha, lambda = lambda,
             media = media, varianza = varia, desv_est = sqrt(varia),
             moda = moda, mediana = log(2)^(1 / alpha) / lambda,
             CV = sqrt(g2 - g1^2) / g1,
             asimetria = (g3 - 3 * g1 * g2 + 2 * g1^3) / (g2 - g1^2)^1.5)
}

parametros <- data.frame(alpha  = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 2.5),
                         lambda = c(1,   1, 1, 1, 1, 0.5))
tabla_carac <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(parametros)),
                       function(i) carac_weibull(parametros$alpha[i], parametros$lambda[i])))
print(round(tabla_carac, 4), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Ejemplo con valores simulados: tiempo de vida de un componente
#    X ~ Weibull(alpha = 2.5, lambda = 0.5), n = 1000
# ---------------------------------------------------------
alpha  <- 2.5
lambda <- 0.5
n      <- 1000

# (a) Con rweibull
x <- rweib(n, alpha, lambda)

# (b) Método de la transformada inversa (Ejercicio 410 del libro):
#     (1/lambda) * (-log(1 - U))^(1/alpha) ~ Weibull(alpha, lambda)
u  <- runif(n)
x2 <- (1 / lambda) * (-log(1 - u))^(1 / alpha)

teo <- carac_weibull(alpha, lambda)


# Moda empírica (máximo de la densidad estimada) vs teórica
d <- density(x)
cat("\nModa teórica:", round(teo$moda, 4), " Moda empírica:", round(d$x[which.max(d$y)], 4), "\n")

# Probabilidad: P(X > 3) exacta vs empírica
cat("P(X > 3) teórica:", round(1 - pweib(3, alpha, lambda), 4),
    " empírica:", mean(x > 3), "\n")

# Histogramas + densidad teórica y distribución empírica vs teórica
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
hist(x, freq = FALSE, breaks = 30, col = "lightblue", border = "white",
     main = "Weibull(2.5, 0.5), n = 1000", xlab = "x", ylab = "Densidad")
curve(dweib(x, alpha, lambda), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, n = 500)
abline(v = c(teo$media, teo$moda), col = c("darkgreen", "purple"), lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
legend("topright", legend = c("Simulación", "PDF teórica", "Media", "Moda"),
       fill = c("lightblue", NA, NA, NA), border = c("white", NA, NA, NA),
       lty = c(NA, 1, 2, 2), col = c(NA, "red", "darkgreen", "purple"),
       lwd = c(NA, 2, 1.5, 1.5), cex = 0.7)

plot(ecdf(x), main = "F empírica vs F teórica", xlab = "x", ylab = "F(x)",
     col = "steelblue", do.points = FALSE, lwd = 2)
curve(pweib(x, alpha, lambda), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2)
legend("bottomright", legend = c("Empírica", "Teórica"),
       col = c("steelblue", "red"), lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Q-Q contra la Weibull teórica y prueba KS
p <- ppoints(n)
plot(qweib(p, alpha, lambda), sort(x), pch = 20, cex = 0.6,
     xlab = "Cuantiles teóricos Weibull", ylab = "Cuantiles muestrales",
     main = "Q-Q: muestra vs Weibull(2.5, 0.5)")
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

print(ks.test(x, "pweibull", shape = alpha, scale = 1 / lambda))

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Verificación del Teorema Central del Límite
#    X_bar ≈ N(mu, sigma/sqrt(n)), con mu y sigma de la Weibull
# ---------------------------------------------------------
mu    <- teo$media
sigma <- teo$desv_est
sk_pob <- teo$asimetria

skewness <- function(x) mean((x - mean(x))^3) / (mean((x - mean(x))^2))^(3/2)
kurtosis <- function(x) mean((x - mean(x))^4) / (mean((x - mean(x))^2))^2

tamanos  <- c(2, 5, 10, 30, 100, 500)
n_medias <- 5000

medias <- lapply(tamanos, function(k) {
  m <- matrix(rweib(k * n_medias, alpha, lambda), nrow = k, ncol = n_medias)
  colMeans(m)
})
names(medias) <- paste0("n=", tamanos)

# Población original
x0 <- rweib(100000, alpha, lambda)
hist(x0, freq = FALSE, breaks = 60, col = "lightgray", border = "white",
     main = "Población: Weibull(2.5, 0.5)", xlab = "x")
curve(dweib(x, alpha, lambda), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Histogramas de las medias + normal teórica
par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (i in seq_along(tamanos)) {
  k <- tamanos[i]
  hist(medias[[i]], freq = FALSE, breaks = 40, col = "lightblue", border = "white",
       main = paste("Medias muestrales, n =", k),
       xlab = "Media muestral", ylab = "Densidad")
  curve(dnorm(x, mean = mu, sd = sigma / sqrt(k)), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2, n = 500)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Gráficos Q-Q
par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (i in seq_along(tamanos)) {
  qqnorm(medias[[i]], main = paste("Q-Q, n =", tamanos[i]), pch = 20, cex = 0.5)
  qqline(medias[[i]], col = "red", lwd = 2)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Medias estandarizadas: Z = (Xbar - mu)/(sigma/sqrt(n)) ~ N(0, 1)
par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (i in seq_along(tamanos)) {
  k <- tamanos[i]
  z <- (medias[[i]] - mu) / (sigma / sqrt(k))
  hist(z, freq = FALSE, breaks = 40, col = "lightgreen", border = "white",
       main = paste("Z estandarizada, n =", k), xlab = "z", xlim = c(-4, 4))
  curve(dnorm(x), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Tabla resumen
resumen <- data.frame(
  n         = tamanos,
  media_obs = sapply(medias, mean),
  media_teo = mu,
  sd_obs    = sapply(medias, sd),
  sd_teo    = sigma / sqrt(tamanos),
  skew_obs  = sapply(medias, skewness),
  skew_teo  = sk_pob / sqrt(tamanos),
  kurt_obs  = sapply(medias, kurtosis),
  KS_D      = sapply(seq_along(tamanos), function(i)
                ks.test(medias[[i]], "pnorm", mean = mu,
                        sd = sigma / sqrt(tamanos[i]))$statistic)
)
comparacion <- data.frame(
  estadistico = c("Media", "Varianza", "Mediana", "CV"),
  teorico = c(teo$media, teo$varianza, teo$mediana, teo$CV),
  rweibull = c(mean(x), var(x), median(x), sd(x) / mean(x)),
  inversa  = c(mean(x2), var(x2), median(x2), sd(x2) / mean(x2))
)

# Redondear solo las columnas numéricas
comparacion[, -1] <- round(comparacion[, -1], 4)
print(comparacion, row.names = FALSE)

# Probabilidad: P(Xbar <= mu + sigma/sqrt(n)) empírica vs normal
comparacion_P <- data.frame(
  n        = tamanos,
  P_emp    = sapply(seq_along(tamanos), function(i)
               mean(medias[[i]] <= mu + sigma / sqrt(tamanos[i]))),
  P_normal = pnorm(1)
)
print(round(comparacion_P, 4), row.names = FALSE)

```
